subcategory: inference-time logic structures (query DAG) instead of pre-built graphs
problem: GraphRAG methods require costly corpus-to-graph construction (token cost, update latency), and a pre-built graph may not match the logical structure each query needs.
architecture: LogicRAG: decomposes the query into subproblems, builds a directed acyclic graph of their logical dependencies, linearises it by topological sort, retrieves for subproblems in order, and applies graph pruning (fewer redundant retrievals) and context pruning (filter irrelevant context).
knowledge_source: passage corpora built from supporting and distractor passages of the selected questions
key_results: 2WikiMQA string accuracy 64.7%, +14.7 points over HippoRAG2; LLM-based accuracy 62.5%.
MuSiQue 30.4% string accuracy vs 27.0% for HippoRAG2.
Query time 9.83 s and 1777.9 tokens on 2WikiMQA vs 35.14 s and 5730.6 tokens for LightRAG, with no offline graph construction.
strengths: Removes the offline graph-building cost while outperforming graph-based RAG baselines.
Same embedding model and LLM for all methods; per-question-type analysis.

limitations.text: The LLM sometimes becomes prematurely confident on long complex queries and answers from partial information (fewer retrieval rounds on harder questions).
Evaluated on 1,000-question subsets with a single generator (GPT-4o-mini).

title: You Don't Need Pre-Built Graphs for RAG: Retrieval Augmented Generation with Adaptive Reasoning Structures
